part.text: Since the buffer is a template, the implementation needs to live in the header. I'll put the template in `circular_buffer.h` and keep the `.cpp` as a thin include.
The `.cpp` already includes the header, which is all it needs since the template lives in the header. Now build and run the tests:

The implementation is complete, but I can't build or run the tests — the shell tool is being denied in this environment.

## What I implemented

**`circular_buffer.h`** — the full solution. Since the tests instantiate `circular_buffer::circular_buffer<int>` and `<std::string>`, the class is a template and must live in the header. It uses:

- A `std::vector<T>` storage with `read_index_`, `write_index_`, and a `size_` counter (all wrapped modulo capacity)
- `write(item)` — throws `std::domain_error` when full
- `overwrite(item)` — when full, advances the read pointer past the oldest item (which sits at the write position) and writes; otherwise behaves like `write`
- `read()` — throws `std::domain_error` when empty, otherwise returns the oldest item
- `clear()` — resets size and both indices

**`circular_buffer.cpp`** — unchanged; it just includes the header, which is all a template needs.

## Verify it

```sh
cmake -S . -B build -DEXERCISM_RUN_ALL_TESTS=ON -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug
cmake --build build
./build/circular-buffer
```
